newsitem.title: USA: U.S. report on Nazi gold to be delayed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. report on Nazi gold to be delayed.

text.p: Publication of a U.S. report on Switzerland's World War II financial dealings with the Nazis has been delayed about two weeks in order to make it more thorough, State Department officials said on Thursday.

The report, which was first announced last October, was originally due to be published on March 27, but is now likely to come out at the end of the first week or in the second week of April, the officials said.

The report is widely expected to be critical of the Swiss wartime role and of a 1946 treaty in which Switzerland agreed to give the allies $58 million to compensate for its handling of gold looted by the Nazi Germans during the war.
U.S. government documents say the Swiss handled more than $400 million in Nazi gold.

The report is being prepared under the supervision of Stuart Eizenstat, currently undersecretary of Commerce for International Trade, but is being compiled from U.S. archives by the State Department's chief historian, William Slany.

State Department officials said that, according to National Archives estimates, some 15 million pages of documents were available on the subject. About 800,000 pages had been declassified in the past year alone, they said.

Slany "feels he needs the extra time to be thorough, and we agree," said one State Department official involved in the project. "We want it to be thorough so that when we issue it, we know that we have captured what happened, we think, in the late 1940s."
The official, who asked not be identified, said the report currently existed in draft form and was circulating around U.S. government agencies.
"As the draft is circulated, what happens is a lot of agencies that have knowledge about this unearth more documents," he said.
Allegations by U.S. Congressmen and Jewish activists that the Swiss profited from their dealings with the Nazis have rocked Switzerland and its secretive banking system in recent months.
In response, the Swiss government announced last month that it would set up a fund to help victims of the Holocaust.
